sources.entry: casey/just: a command runner written in Rust (claims to be better than Makefile)

summary.one_liner: just is a command runner written in Rust that saves and runs project-specific commands ("recipes") defined in a justfile, with make-inspired syntax.
summary.what_it_does: The tool reads recipes from a file named justfile (case-insensitive, searched in the current directory and upward) and runs them with `just RECIPE`. Recipes can take positional, variadic, option, and flag arguments, declare dependencies (prior and subsequent), and run in parallel with the [parallel] attribute. It supports variables, expressions, string functions, .env loading, and organizing justfiles into modules and imports. Recipes can be listed with --list, grouped with attributes, and documented with comments. The README also describes shell and PowerShell configuration, optional unstable features gated by a flag, and editor and language-server support.
use_cases: save project-specific shell commands for a repo
replace makefile-style task running with a simpler runner
run tests, builds, or deploy steps with one short command
run project tasks on Windows with PowerShell or cmd
run tasks in CI pipelines such as GitHub Actions
how_to_run: Download a pre-built binary from the releases page
Create a file named justfile in your project root with recipes
stack: sh (or a configured shell such as PowerShell or cmd.exe)
notable: Recipes can be written in any language, such as Python or Node.js, not only shell
Errors such as unknown recipes and circular dependencies are reported before anything runs
Backwards-compatibility commitment since version 1.0, with opt-in changes per justfile
Installable through many package managers and as a Docker image, plus a Node.js wrapper package
Editor support for Vim, Neovim, Emacs, VS Code, Helix, and others, plus a language server
caveats: Requires a POSIX-like sh on Windows (for example from Git for Windows or Cygwin) unless you set a different shell
Some features are unstable and produce an error unless the --unstable flag or set unstable is used
Positional arguments behave differently under PowerShell, so enabling them may break PowerShell recipes
